United States.text: Its first golf course, Oakhurst Links in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, was a nine-hole course built in 1884.
United States.evidence: Oakhurst Links is a historic golf course located at White Sulphur Springs, Greenbrier County, West Virginia. It was the first golf course in the United States. It is a nine-hole course built in 1884, in a design based upon traditional Scottish design elements.

Japan.text: Its first golf course was laid out on Mount Rokko, above Kobe, in 1903 by an English expatriate, Arthur Groom.
Japan.evidence: The Kobe Golf Club ... is Japan's first golf course, built on Mount Rokko in 1903 by English expatriate Arthur Hasketh Groom.

Canada.text: Royal Montreal, founded in 1873, is the oldest golf club in North America still in existence.
Canada.evidence: It is the second-oldest golf club in North America, (the oldest being The Savannah Golf Club, in Savannah, Georgia, USA; established in 1794) and the oldest in continuous existence.

England.text: Its oldest golf course, at Westward Ho! in Devon, dates from 1864.
England.evidence: Founded in 1864 as the North Devon and West of England Golf Club, RND operates the oldest golf course in England.

Australia.text: Royal Melbourne, founded in 1891, is its oldest club still going, and its West course ranks in the world's top five.
Australia.evidence: Founded 135 years ago in 1891, it is Australia's oldest extant and continually existing golf club. ... The West course is ranked in the top-five courses in the world.

Germany.text: Its Bernhard Langer was golf's first official world No. 1, in 1986, a year after winning the Masters.
Germany.evidence: In 1986, he became the sport's first number one ranked player following the creation of the Sony Ranking (now the Official World Golf Ranking). His first major win came at the 1985 Masters Tournament

France.text: The Pau Golf Club, opened in 1856, is the oldest in continental Europe; it hired France's first golf professional in 1883.
France.evidence: The Pau Golf Club is the oldest club in continental Europe. ... The Pau Golf Club hired the first professional golfer in France, Joe Lloyd, in 1883.

South Korea.text: Golf is a status symbol there: club membership costs far more than in Japan or the US, and 47 Koreans play on the women's LPGA Tour.
South Korea.evidence: Golf is very popular in South Korea. It is often thought that this is linked to the fact that golf is considered a status symbol. Membership in golf clubs in South Korea is considerably more expensive than in Japan or the US. South Korea is especially strong in women's golf; 47 Koreans play on the world's leading women's tour, the LPGA Tour.

Sweden.text: Golf boomed there in the 1980s, when its courses nearly doubled in a decade; it now has over half a million players.
Sweden.evidence: Golf boomed in the 1980s, and the number of courses almost doubled in a single decade to 271. ... Today it is a popular sport with over half a million active players and close to 500 courses.

Scotland.text: The word 'golf' first appears in an act of the Scots Parliament of 1457, and Musselburgh claims the world's oldest course still played.
Scotland.evidence: The word golf was first recorded in the 15th century, appearing twice in an act of the Scots Parliament of 6 March 1457, in the reign of James II. ... The Old Links at Musselburgh Racecourse is claimed to be the oldest playing golf course in the world.
